text.p: A strong earthquake shook Mexico City on Saturday afternoon, setting off car alarms and sending inhabitants running out into the street.
There were no immediate reports of injuries or damage.
The quake shook Mexico City at around 2:30 p.m. (2030 GMT) and was felt all over the city, sending some small objects falling from shelves in houses.
Radio reports said the tremor had also been felt in Mexico's second city of Guadalajara in the west of the country.

In the first minutes after the quake, private network Radio Red said it had no reports of damage to buildings in the Mexican capital but added that it was too soon to be certain what might have happened.
Electricity and telephone services appeared to be working normally in most parts of the capital.
